**Meeting and Attendance**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, October 15, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; it adjourned at 8:11 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary. Present besides Mr. Schmidt: Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson; Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Foren, and Trudel. Approximately 25 members of the audience attended.

**Recognition and Mission Moment**
Student Spotlight recognized creative achievement in the TSD Creative Guild; Thomas Butcher introduced Athens senior Maisie Justes and described her journey as a filmmaker. The U.S. Department of Education designates October as Learning Disabilities / Dyslexia / ADHD / Down Syndrome Awareness Month; Governor Whitmer declared October Learning Disabilities Month in Michigan.

**Resolutions adopted**

| Resolution | Moved by | Supported by | Vote |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Learning Disabilities Awareness Month, October 2024 | Dr. Wilson | Dr. Philippart | Yes 7 / No 0 |
| Principal Appreciation Month | Mrs. Alic | Mr. Haupt | Yes 7 / No 0 |
| 2025 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists | Dr. Philippart | Mrs. Alic | Yes 7 / No 0 |

The Learning Disabilities resolution notes that 1 in 5 individuals have a learning disability and joins Governor Gretchen Whitmer in commemorating October 2024 as Learning Disabilities Month in Michigan.

**NSPRA Awards**
The Communications Department received 11 national awards through the NSPRA National School Communication Awards: 6 Awards of Excellence, 4 Awards of Merit, and 1 Honorable Mention. Excellence: Troy Union At a Glance Infographic; Elevating Voices: In Comfortably Uncomfortable Conversations Podcast; Discover Kitchen Cookoff Video; Positive Behavior Incentive Systems at Morse Elementary School Video; Why You Should Take a Music Class in Middle School Video; The Press Room on our Website. Merit: Inside TSD with Dr. Rich Machesky Podcast; TSD Weekly Newsletter; Magic of Light at Hamilton Video; Why Flexible Seating Video. Honorable Mention: the district newspaper mailed to homes 3 to 4 times per year inside the Troy Times.

**National Merit**
More than one million students nationwide, from some 21,000 high schools, entered the National Merit Scholarship Program; approximately 16,000 seniors are selected as semifinalists. Troy had sixty-nine, whose names Mrs. Anne read aloud. Semifinalist status requires scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT with comparable SAT scores. Copies of the resolution will be presented at a reception on November 7th.

**Consent Agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Dr. Philippart; items A through E: minutes of the September 3, 2024 Workshop; minutes of the September 17, 2024 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report - August 2024; Oakland County Special Education Parent Advisory Committee Representatives; and OCSBA Bylaws Amendment. Yes 7, No 0.

**Business**

| Item | Party / Fund | Amount | Moved / Supported | Vote |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New Smith Middle School construction (architectural, mechanical, electrical, civil/site) | Capital Projects Fund, Sinking Fund, Food Services Fund | $8,915,483.00 | Anne / Haupt | Yes 7 / No 0 |
| Cafeteria tables, Leonard Elementary School | Great Lakes Furniture Supply, Inc.; 2023 Bond Fund | $48,530.00 | Haupt / Hauff | Yes 7 / No 0 |

**Student Representatives and Board Comments**
Reports came from Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School), Madie Miller (Troy High School, filling in for Adam McManus, absent), Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East), and Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School). Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop in the Administration Building on November 12th at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting on October 21st in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m., and reminded everyone to vote in the district's millage renewal election on November 5th. Additions and Deletions, Public Communication (agenda and non-agenda), Personnel, Curriculum, and Other were all recorded as None.
2024_150_m101524bdmtg.verbose:
**Meeting identification.** Minutes of a Board Meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held October 15, 2024 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The meeting of the Troy Board of Education was held at the Troy School District Services Building located at 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Foren, and Trudel. There were approximately 25 members of the audience. The meeting adjourned at 8:11 p.m. The minutes are respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation GH/jh.

**Recognition - Student Spotlight.** The Board introduced the evening's Student Spotlight, the segment in which students are recognized for creative achievements they accomplish in the TSD Creative Guild. The Board invited Thomas Butcher to the podium to introduce Athens senior Maisie Justes and to share about her success in her journey as a filmmaker.

**Mission Moment - Learning Disabilities Awareness Month.** National associations for a number of different learning differences have each declared October as an awareness month, including associations for Dyslexia, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, and Down Syndrome. To honor and magnify those efforts, the U.S. Department of Education has declared October as Learning Disabilities / Dyslexia / Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder / Down Syndrome Awareness Month. In Michigan, Governor Whitmer provided a more encompassing definition and declared October as Learning Disabilities Month, and the Troy Board of Education adopted its own resolution in response.

The resolution, titled Learning Disabilities Awareness Month, October 2024, was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart. Its recitals state that the term learning disabilities refers to differences in how our brains work, which may affect the acquisition, organization, retention, understanding, or use of verbal or nonverbal information; that learning disabilities range in severity and may impact the acquisition and use of oral language, reading, written language, and mathematics; that 1 in 5 individuals have a learning disability; that learning disabilities may co-exist with other disabilities and conditions and can affect individuals regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, or other intersecting factors; that disabilities are a natural part of human diversity but individuals with learning disabilities may face discrimination or marginalization; that every person has strengths and learning disabilities should not keep individuals from realizing their full potential; that specialized assessments and interventions involving home, school, community, and workplace settings can significantly enhance quality of life; that appropriate supports and services allow individuals with learning disabilities to achieve their goals and participate fully in society; and that celebrating unique abilities is essential to an inclusive society embracing the potential of all Michigan residents. The resolving clause has the Troy School District Board of Education join Governor Gretchen Whitmer in commemorating October 2024 as Learning Disabilities Month in Michigan. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Resolution adopted.

**Principal Appreciation Month.** Throughout the State of Michigan, October has traditionally been celebrated as Principal Appreciation Month in recognition of the work of building-level educational leaders. The resolution commending elementary and secondary principals was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt. Its recitals state that energetic and inspiring school leadership is essential if teachers, schools, and districts are to ensure that all Troy students are college and career ready; that K-12 school principals play a vital role in student success and act as liaison between the school and the community it serves, ensuring parents and the community are aware of student and school achievements; that Troy School District principals are dedicated, quality educational professionals committed to providing sound leadership and guidance to their staff and students; and that during this month the district joins educators, parents, and students throughout Michigan to raise awareness of the importance of educational leadership and to thank all principals working in Troy. The resolving clause officially recognizes October as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Resolution adopted.

**2024 National School Public Relations Association (NSPRA) Awards.** The Board recognized the Troy School District Communications Department and invited them forward. The Communications team received 11 national awards this year through the National School Public Relations Association National School Communication Awards: 6 Awards of Excellence, 4 Awards of Merit, and 1 Honorable Mention. The Awards of Excellence were for the Troy Union At a Glance Infographic; Elevating Voices: In Comfortably Uncomfortable Conversations Podcast; the Discover Kitchen Cookoff Video; the Positive Behavior Incentive Systems at Morse Elementary School Video; the Why You Should Take a Music Class in Middle School Video; and The Press Room on the district website. The Awards of Merit were for the Inside TSD with Dr. Rich Machesky Podcast; the TSD Weekly Newsletter; the Magic of Light at Hamilton Video; and the Why Flexible Seating Video. The Award of Honorable Mention was for the Troy School District newspaper that is mailed to homes 3 to 4 times per year inside the Troy Times. The team received the awards over the summer, certificates were displayed on screens around the room, and the Communications Team had already hung the awards down the hallway to the studio. The Board expressed pride in the department's creative talent and its work strengthening the bond between the schools and the community.

**2025 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists.** More than one million students nationwide, from some 21,000 high schools, entered the National Merit Scholarship Program this year; approximately 16,000 of these seniors are selected to be semifinalists. The Board passed a resolution to commend and congratulate the district's sixty-nine National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists. Mrs. Anne read the names of the following students: Aleezay Ahmad, Nurayda Albeez, Gurgia Bains, Jacob Baker, Arin Barman, David Chen, Terence Chen, Saanvi Duruvasan, Akhilan Ganeshkumar, Octavian German, Sriram Yeshaswi Godugula, Adwayan Goswami, David He, Erin Jeong, Lillian Jing, Sophia Kaltsounis, Atiksh Karanwal, Jeffrey Kim, Krrish Kishore Kumar, Arjun Korrakuti, Pranavi Kumar, Anthony Li, Matthew Li, Michael Li, Edison Lin, Pelon Lin, Ethan Liu, Rishi Lokesh, Suraj Makunur, Arjun Manyem, Brenda Mao, Claire Mao, Nishka Mehta, Joseph Morelli, Vandya Nedle, Kevin Oakes, Ritesh Palla, Rhea Pawar, Rahul Perala, Elizabeth Pfauth, Rohith Pramod, Vishnav Ramesh, Rishabh Rao, Sri Sowmya Sanka, Swathi Seshadri, Aaditya Shah, Kalp Shah, Tanay Shah, Shamanth Shastry, Benjamin Sheng, Shabd Shienh, Abhradeep Shil, Sanjay Shyamsundar, Arnav Sinha, Athrv Siriki, Parnavi Sonar, JoAnn Tu, Alexander Ulrich, Aryan Vadlamudi, Ajay Varghese, Sanjeevkumar Vijayakumar, Aishwarya Viswanathan, Ryan Wang, Jessica Wu, Olivia Xu, Elaine Zhang, Yuchen Zhang, Zhedong Zhao, and Angela Zhou. The minutes call this a remarkable number of semifinalists and a tribute to the staff and parents of the Troy School District. Copies of the resolution will be presented to the students at a reception on November 7th. The resolution was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic; its recitals note that student achievement is honored through the National Merit semifinalist and finalist recognition programs and that National Merit students reach semifinalist status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test (PSAT) and earning comparable scores on the Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT). Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Resolution adopted.

**Additions and Deletions; Public Communication (Agenda Items).** Both recorded as None.

**General - Consent Agenda.** It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B, C, D, and E on the consent agenda: minutes of the September 3, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the September 17, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - August 2024; Oakland County Special Education Parent Advisory Committee Representatives; and OCSBA Bylaws Amendment. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Personnel and Curriculum.** Both sections recorded as None.

**Business - New Smith Middle School Construction Items.** It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Haupt that the bid for the construction of a new Smith Middle School, including architectural, mechanical, electrical and civil/site work, be awarded as attached in the amount of $8,915,483.00, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund, Sinking Fund, and Food Services Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Business - Cafeteria Tables, Leonard Elementary School.** It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mr. Hauff that the purchase of cafeteria tables be awarded to Great Lakes Furniture Supply, Inc. in the amount of $48,530.00, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Bond Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items) and Other.** Both recorded as None.

**Reports from High School Student Representatives.** Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Madie Miller, student representative for Troy High School, filled in for Adam McManus, who was not present, and shared a report on events and activities at her school. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, shared a report on events and activities at his school.

**Board Comments and Adjournment.** Board members shared upcoming events of possible community interest. Mr. Schmidt announced that the next Board Workshop would be held in the Administration Building on November 12th at 6:00 p.m. and that the next regular meeting would be held on October 21st in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m. He also reminded everyone to vote at the upcoming election for the district's millage renewal on November 5th. The meeting adjourned at 8:11 p.m.
